questions.question: Which statement best defines a Request for Comments (RFC) and includes correct examples of protocols it defines?

options.A: An informal blog post about networking; examples: HTML, CSS
options.B: A standard‑setting document published by the IETF that details technical specifications; examples: TCP, IP, HTTP, SMTP
options.C: A hardware manual for routers; examples: Ethernet, WiFi
options.D: A proprietary software license; examples: Windows, macOS

questions.explanation:
RFCs are technical standards documents from the IETF that define protocols such as TCP, IP, HTTP, and SMTP. [Page 5]

---

questions.question: How does the Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF) contribute to protocol standards?

options.A: By manufacturing network cables for Ethernet
options.B: By developing and publishing standards documents such as RFCs that describe how protocols should operate
options.C: By certifying WiFi devices for consumer use
options.D: By allocating IP address blocks to end users

questions.explanation:
The IETF develops Internet standards through RFCs, ensuring agreement on protocol behavior. [Page 5]

---

questions.question: Which of the following correctly defines the IEEE 802 standards committee and provides examples of standards it specifies?

options.A: A group that writes software APIs; examples: Java, .NET
options.B: An organization that defines link‑layer standards for LANs; examples: Ethernet and WiFi
options.C: A consortium that creates encryption algorithms; examples: AES, RSA
options.D: A standards body for satellite communications; examples: GPS, GLONASS

questions.explanation:
IEEE 802 is noted for specifying Ethernet and wireless WiFi standards. [Page 5]

---

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of protocol layering in network design?

options.A: To increase the physical size of network devices
options.B: To organize protocols into hierarchical layers so each layer provides services to the one above and uses services from the one below
options.C: To merge all network functions into a single monolithic protocol
options.D: To eliminate the need for standards bodies

questions.explanation:
Layering structures protocols so that each belongs to a layer, providing and consuming services. [Page 49]

---

questions.question: Which description accurately defines the Internet Protocol (IP) as presented in the context?

options.A: A transport‑layer protocol that guarantees ordered delivery of data streams
options.B: A link‑layer protocol that defines WiFi channel access methods
options.C: A network‑layer protocol that specifies the format of packets exchanged among routers and end systems
options.D: An application‑layer protocol used for sending email

questions.explanation:
IP is described as specifying packet format at the network layer. [Page 5]

---

questions.question: How does the Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) differ from link‑layer reliable delivery services?

options.A: TCP provides end‑to‑end reliable delivery between two hosts, while link‑layer reliability is limited to a single hop between directly connected devices
options.B: TCP encrypts all data, whereas link‑layer services do not
options.C: TCP operates only on wireless networks, while link‑layer services work only on wired networks
options.D: TCP is defined by IEEE 802, while link‑layer reliability is defined by the IETF

questions.explanation:
TCP offers reliable delivery from one end system to another, unlike link‑layer reliability which is hop‑by‑hop. [Page 51]

---

questions.question: Which of the following best defines a link‑layer protocol and gives correct examples?

options.A: A protocol that routes packets across the Internet; examples: BGP, OSPF
options.B: A protocol that provides reliable end‑to‑end data streams; examples: TCP, SCTP
options.C: A protocol that operates at the data link layer to control how bits are transmitted over a physical medium; examples: Ethernet, WiFi, DOCSIS
options.D: A protocol for formatting web pages; examples: HTML, CSS

questions.explanation:
Link‑layer protocols include Ethernet, WiFi, and DOCSIS as examples. [Page 51]

---

questions.question: In the context of the network layer, why is the IP protocol referred to as “the glue that binds the Internet together”?

options.A: Because it physically connects cables in a network hub
options.B: Because it provides the common addressing and packet format that all higher‑layer protocols rely on for communication across diverse networks
options.C: Because it encrypts all traffic on the Internet
options.D: Because it supplies power to network devices

questions.explanation:
IP’s role as the fundamental protocol at the network layer makes it the “glue” for Internet connectivity. [Page 51]

---

questions.question: Which statement accurately defines “protocol standards” and explains why they are important for interoperability?

options.A: Protocol standards are optional guidelines that manufacturers may ignore; they have no impact on device compatibility.
options.B: Protocol standards are detailed specifications that describe exactly how protocols should behave, enabling different systems and products to work together reliably.
options.C: Protocol standards are marketing terms used to sell networking equipment at higher prices.
options.D: Protocol standards are only relevant for wireless networks, not wired ones.

questions.explanation:
Standards ensure agreement on protocol behavior for interoperable systems. [Page 5]

---

questions.question: Which description correctly defines the TCP/IP suite and lists its primary constituent protocols?

options.A: A collection of application‑layer protocols only; examples: HTTP, SMTP, FTP
options.B: A set of networking standards that includes the Transport Control Protocol and Internet Protocol as core components, along with related protocols such as TCP, IP, HTTP, and SMTP
options.C: A hardware specification for network interface cards
options.D: A wireless communication protocol used for satellite links

questions.explanation: The TCP/IP suite encompasses TCP, IP, HTTP, and SMTP among others. [Page 5]
